newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Mixed deals struck in ASDA, C&W.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Mixed deals struck in ASDA, C&W.

text.p: An appetite for UK food retailing shares on Tuesday spilled over onto the traded options of ASDA Group Plc, where the main deals were mixed, dealers said.

On the bullish side was the deal to buy 1,000 October 110 calls at 9-1/2p in the supermarket chain. The deal will only be profitable if the underlying shares go up, and if the calls are held to expiry, the shares need to go above 119-1/2p.

Apart from gearing -- or the ability of options to make large percentage gains from a modest rise in the underlying shares -- the purchaser may have a view to buying the stock but only if the shares can demonstrate they are trending higher. To this end, once the options are in-the-money, the calls may be exercised anytime upto the expiry date. And if the shares tumble, the maximum loss will only be that from buying the calls and this may be less than had the shares been bought.

Alternatvely, the purchaser may have bought the options expecting to allocate money for a share purchase at some time in the future but needs to buy calls now in case the share price rallies and the opportunity is lost to buy the shares at a lower price.
Another large trade in Asda was a neutral position from the sale of 750 July 110 calls and puts at 7-1/2p and 4-1/2p each.
This short straddle strategy will make a maximum of 12p profit if Asda shares are 110p at expiry.
By 1340 GMT, ASDA shares were up 4-3/4p at 112-1/4p.
Elsewhere, in telecommunications group Cable & Wireless the main deal was the rolling forward of a bearish position.
The deal was to sell 2,500 April 500 puts at 8p to close an existing position and to buy 2,500 July 500 puts at 31p.
